## Figure 1.22: Bond Buyback in Low- and Middle-Income Countries, 2025
Horizontal bar chart.

- **Units:** US$ (million)
- **Time span:** 2025
- **X-axis:** US$ (million), ranging from **0** to **20,000**, with ticks at **2,000** intervals
- **Y-axis:** Countries
- **Series/legend:** Single series showing bond buyback amounts by country
- **Countries shown:** Mexico, Colombia, Argentina, Dominican Republic, Kenya, Peru, Côte d’Ivoire, Mongolia, Indonesia, Suriname, Jordan, Paraguay, Benin, Gabon

### Values
| Country | Bond buyback (US$ million) |
|---|---:|
| Mexico | 17,618 |
| Colombia | 6,606 |
| Argentina | 2,816 |
| Dominican Republic | 1,818 |
| Kenya | 1,208 |
| Peru | 1,080 |
| Côte d’Ivoire | 759 |
| Mongolia | 500 |
| Indonesia | 462 |
| Suriname | 420 |
| Jordan | 388 |
| Paraguay | 300 |
| Benin | 261 |
| Gabon | 225 |

### Rankings and visual comparisons
- **Largest:** Mexico (**17,618**), by a wide margin.
- **Second largest:** Colombia (**6,606**).
- **Third largest:** Argentina (**2,816**).
- **Smallest:** Gabon (**225**).
- Mexico’s buyback is well over twice Colombia’s and far exceeds all other countries shown.
- Colombia’s amount is more than double Argentina’s.
- The **Dominican Republic (1,818)**, **Kenya (1,208)**, and **Peru (1,080)** form the next tier after Argentina.
- All remaining countries are below **US$ 1 billion**, except Kenya and Peru, which are just above **US$ 1 billion**.
- No negative values are shown.

**Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
